canonicalText: Civic Hall announced a New York City Council constituent-services hackathon for January 30, 2016, from 1-3 p.m.
publicProjection: Civic Hall announced the January 30, 2016 event for 1-3 p.m. and described it as focused on improving constituent services.
boundaries: Describe 1-3 p.m. as announced hours, not proven event duration.
antiClaims: The event necessarily began and ended at the announced times.

canonicalText: The New York City Council described the January 30, 2016 gathering at Civic Hall as its first CouncilStat hackathon.
publicProjection: On January 30, 2016, the New York City Council held its first CouncilStat hackathon at Civic Hall.
antiClaims: The event was the Council's first civic-data hackathon.
The event was the Council's first hackathon of any kind.

canonicalText: The promotional graphic attached to Civic Hall's announcement reads 'New York City Council Hackathon.'
publicProjection: The Council-branded graphic attached to Civic Hall's announcement used the wording 'New York City Council Hackathon.'
boundaries: Treat the wording as promotional branding, not a formal registration title.
antiClaims: The graphic proves a longer official event title.

canonicalText: After CouncilStat constituent-services data became publicly available, Jamie independently developed CallNYC.org as a resident-facing civic-data prototype; Politico New York covered it in March 2016.
publicProjection: After CouncilStat constituent-services data became publicly available, Jamie independently developed CallNYC.org as an archived resident-facing civic-data prototype. Politico New York covered the project in March 2016.
boundaries: CallNYC was an independent follow-on project, not an official Council product or current service.
antiClaims: Jamie built CallNYC at the hackathon.
CallNYC is a current public-service directory.

canonicalText: Participant photographs show a breakout placard reading 'Digital District - Help improve City Council District office operations.'
publicProjection: Participant photographs document a Digital District breakout placard.
boundaries: Do not project publicly until image rights, crop, credit, and represented-person review are complete.
antiClaims: Digital District was the formal title of the whole event.
